text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. However, most APIs require authentication, such as an API key or token, to confirm your identity. You should also be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, good error handling is essential, because requests can fail for many reasons, and your program should respond gracefully.
